title: Affine neighbourhoods on separated almost homogeneous schemes over a semi-trait
statement: A semi-trait here is $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, where $R$ is a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] of Krull dimension one (every strict chain of prime ideals has length at most one, and a chain of length one exists) with finitely many maximal ideals; in particular a trait is allowed. A group sheaf takes values in groups, not necessarily commutative. A group scheme has multiplication, identity and inverse morphisms satisfying the group identities. Let $G\to S$ be a separated flat group scheme of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $X\to S$ be a separated flat scheme of finite presentation with a $G$-action. Flatness is [def-weil-flat-morphism]; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Suppose $X$ is a finite union of $G$-invariant open subschemes $X_j$ such that $(g,x)\mapsto(gx,x)$ from $G\times_S X_j$ to $X_j\times_S X_j$ is surjective as a morphism of fppf sheaves: any pair of sections over a test scheme becomes of this form on an fppf covering [def-pc-fppf-site]. Empty fibres of $X_j$ are allowed. Then $X$ has property (FA). Property (FA) means that every finite subset of the underlying point set is contained in an affine open subscheme.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.2 and Definition 4.0.1, printed pp.53-54 and 57-59; almost homogeneous separated schemes, including the non-smooth case via Proposition 4.2.3. The assertion for components supported only on the generic fibre is the field case in 4.1. Local archive WANTED; primary scan https://www.numdam.org/article/MSMF_1973__33__5_0.pdf

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-almost-homogeneous-potential-smooth-cover] to $S,G,X$ and the given finite invariant cover. Obtain $T,H,Y$ and $q:Y\to X$ with the stated smoothness, geometric orbit decomposition, integrality, surjectivity and finite fibres. In particular $T$ is the spectrum of a Noetherian normal dimension-one domain. The finite-presentation hypothesis on $X\to S$ includes finite type; hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian, so it is a locally Noetherian target for the later neighbourhood-transfer lemma. We will not require $q$ to be flat or finite.

Apply [lem-sfb-dedekind-smooth-fibre-dense-affine] to the smooth separated finite-type map $Y\to T$. It gives an affine open $U\subseteq Y$ whose pullback is dense in every geometric fibre of $Y\to T$. These hypotheses hold for the ring of $T$ by step 1. We use only the affine open and geometric density, not the additional Cartier divisor supplied by that lemma.

source.place: 4.2.2 smooth-case proof, printed p.57, affine open containing fibre-maximal points; existing BLR fibre-dense-affine input

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-connected-action-affine-saturation-ample] to $H,Y,U$ over the affine normal Noetherian base $T$. Its group and scheme are smooth, separated and of finite type by step 1, and the fibres of $H$ are geometrically connected. Thus $W=H.U$ is open and admits an ample invertible module. In fact $W=Y$. To check this, pass to any geometric fibre. Every nonempty orbit in that fibre is open by step 1, so density of $U$ forces it to meet $U$. Given a geometric point $y$ in this orbit, take a point of the nonempty intersection after extending the algebraically closed field if necessary. The orbit clause in step 1 supplies $h$ carrying that point of $U$ to $y$ over a common algebraically closed extension. Hence $y$ lies in the image of $H\times_TU\to Y$ on points. Every point of $Y$ has a geometric lift, so all points lie in $W$. Equality of underlying open sets identifies their open subschemes. Consequently the ample module on $W$ is an ample module on $Y$. The same argument covers a fibre with several orbits and is vacuous on an empty fibre.

source.place: 4.2.2 smooth-case proof, printed p.57, equality of the neutral-component saturation with the whole space and the quoted ampleness proposition

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary finite subset $E\subseteq|X|$. Because each underlying fibre of $q$ is finite, $E'=q^{-1}(E)$ is a finite union of finite sets and hence finite. Step 3 gives an ample invertible module on $Y$. By [lem-sc-ample-finite-set-affine], there exists an affine open $V\subseteq Y$ containing all of $E'$, not just a chosen lift of each member of $E$.

source.place: 4.2.2 smooth-case conclusion quasi-projective, printed p.57; finite-set consequence Stacks Tag 01ZY (properties-lemma-ample-finite-set-in-affine)

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-integral-finite-fibre-affine-neighbourhood-transfer] for $q:Y\to X$ and $E$. The target is locally Noetherian by step 1; integrality, surjectivity and finite fibres are supplied by the potential-smooth-cover statement. Step 4 supplies precisely its inverse-image neighbourhood hypothesis. Therefore $E$ lies in an affine open of $X$. Since $E$ was arbitrary, this is property (FA), including the empty-set case.

proof_origin.place: 4.2.2 proof, printed pp.57–59; local archive WANTED, primary scan read online. Assembly follows the published proof with the existing BLR fibre-dense-affine lemma, and spells out orbit saturation and finite inverse images.

New nodes against source: 4.1.3 (OCR 4.1.5, p.55) matches the transfer node verbatim; it has no flatness hypothesis, so it is not a duplicate of the flat integral-fpqc-descent node. Raynaud V.3.10 as quoted on p.57 (locally Noetherian normal S, smooth group with connected fibres, smooth X, U quasi-affine, O(D) S-ample on G.U) implies the saturation node's specialization: affine U over an affine base gives an absolutely ample module, and W is open because the action is smooth. 4.2.3 (i),(ii) and its last paragraph (pp.58-59) give the cover node with H=G1^0 and Y=X1. Krull-Akizuki gives a semilocal Noetherian R' with finite fibres; q is a finite normalization composed with an integral base change, so it is integral, surjective with finite fibres. The geometric orbit clause follows from fppf almost-homogeneity under the connected H_Omega. Steps: 1, the hypotheses and local Noetherianity of X hold. 2, only the fibre-dense affine is used, matching the source's affine open containing the fibre-maximal points. 3, G0.U = X is written out correctly from orbit openness and density. 4, E' is finite and 01ZY applies. 5, 4.1.3 applies to the whole inverse image. Edge cases checked: empty X, empty or generic-only fibres, several orbits, the non-smooth alpha_p/mu_p cases, and non-flat thickenings. No node restates the item.
